architecture.mechanism: Incorporation of an advanced graphite additive into the lead negative electrode to suppress irreversible lead sulfate crystallization during deep discharge events.
architecture.intervention: Reformulate the negative plate paste of the 12V lead-acid starter battery by adding a conductive carbon-graphite additive compatible with standard flooded or AGM cell construction, maintaining identical physical dimensions and terminal specifications so the battery operates within the factory Subaru electrical system and alternator charging output parameters (13.5-14.7V).
architecture.expected_effect: The graphite additive maintains electrical percolation pathways within the negative active mass during deep discharge, preventing the formation of large, irreversible lead sulfate crystals that cause capacity fade, thereby allowing the battery to recover full cranking amperage after accidental deep discharge events such as leaving accessories on.
architecture.falsification_test: Subject both the graphite-modified battery and a standard OEM-specification battery to five consecutive 100% depth-of-discharge cycles at C/20 rate followed by standard 14.4V constant-voltage recharge simulating the Subaru alternator output; if the modified battery does not demonstrate statistically significant higher recovered cold cranking amps and lower internal resistance than the control battery, the mechanism is falsified.
